assumptions: Source definition: the NIST footnote expressly identifies the DC reciprocal relationship.

Application profile: a finite positive passive ohmic resistance and its corresponding conductance at matching conditions. The reciprocal definition alone does not establish that a physical device is ohmic.

gaps: Add S and electrical_conductance; ohm and electrical_resistance already proposed in batch 01 but still unsupported by the runtime.
Do not alias this component quantity to electrical_conductivity or to a negative differential-conductance quantity. Instance compatibility remains contextual.

models.inverse_notes: Solve R from known G: R=1/G, requiring finite G>0 and recovered R>0 as in the original guard. G=0.125 S gives R=8 ohm and forward substitution gives 0.125 S. G=0 has no finite R; it represents only an open-circuit limit. R=0 likewise has no finite G. Every admissible inverse has one value and no root branch. A conductance value cannot supply component identity, temperature or a valid ohmic range.
limitations: This profile excludes ideal zero resistance, infinite resistance and active negative resistance. An ideal open circuit has G=0 only as an infinite-resistance limit, not a finite input here.

G is measured in S and is not the bulk conductivity sigma in S/m. The SOP surrounding text mixes conductivity and conductance terminology and its AC wording is not used. No empirical fit or apparatus calibration is supplied by this definition.

references.method: Oracle derived from published voltage/current data: 0.003 A / 9.00 V = 1/3000 S, not a published G result. Published R=3.00 kilohms is converted to 3000 ohm. Input rounding +/-5 ohm plus the independent I/V rounding (I +/-0.000005 A, V +/-0.005 V) gives a combined allowance below 1.30e-6 S; 1.31e-6 S bounds it.
references.provenance: openstax-ohmic-example, Example 9.8(a). The source inferred R from the same tuple; this alternate ratio is an arithmetic/definition check, not independent laboratory validation.

references.method: Independent unit-response construction: an ideal linear component conducts 0.75 A at 6 V, so each volt corresponds to 0.125 A. Its separately expressed V/I resistance is 8 ohm. This obtains expected conductance from response per volt. Synthetic exact values; numerical-only tolerance.
references.provenance: Curator independent definition check using NIST siemens=A/V and the source ohmic interpretation.

rejection_cases.reason: Original reciprocal denominator is zero; an ideal short has no finite G in this format.
Active negative resistance is outside the declared passive application profile.

assumptions: Source flux law: I is the oriented surface integral of current density (Eq. 9.5). Derived definition: divide that integral by its positive surface area.

Application profile: stationary surface in a DC state. A local-current interpretation additionally requires the normal component to be uniform; interpretation as a positive magnitude additionally requires aligned positive normal flow. Neither condition is needed for the area mean.

gaps: Add A, m^2, A/m^2, surface_area and area_mean_normal_current_density. electric_current retains the prior steady signed meaning.
The surface mean is a new derived quantity. Do not bind it to local current-density magnitude or a time average without a validated spatial/temporal mapping.

models.inverse_notes: Solve I given J_mean_n,A: I=J_mean_n*A, requiring A>0; -300 A/m^2 and 0.0004 m^2 give -0.12 A and substitution returns -300. J_mean_n=0 gives unique I=0 for any known valid area. Solve A given I,J_mean_n: A=I/J_mean_n, requiring J_mean_n!=0 and recovered A>0, so nonzero I and the mean must have the same sign. I=-0.12 A,J_mean_n=-300 A/m^2 gives 0.0004 m^2. I=0,J_mean_n=0 leaves all positive areas possible; zero mean with nonzero current is inconsistent. Zero current with nonzero mean returns inadmissible zero area. Inverses are single valued when admissible and nonsingular; neither determines the shape of the surface or local field.
limitations: This scalar output does not reconstruct the spatial field, tangential current, local maxima or a current-density vector. Zero mean need not mean zero local motion or heating.

Surface orientation and area support must match the current measurement. surface_area is broader than batch-01 cross_sectional_area; a binding is valid only when both describe the same actual transverse surface.

references.method: Published expected 1.65e5 A/m^2 is retained. Convert source area 5.26 mm^2 to 5.26e-6 m^2. Under its uniform positive normal-flow example, magnitude equals the introduced mean. Half-last-digit I and A bounds are 0.005 A and 0.005e-6 m^2; propagated input change is below 1110 A/m^2. Add 500 A/m^2 output rounding; 1620 A/m^2 bounds the comparison.
references.provenance: openstax-current-density, Example 9.4; source area is used directly, without recomputing a rounded diameter.

references.method: Independent spatial-average construction: patches of 1e-4 and 3e-4 m^2 carry normal densities -600 and -200 A/m^2. Their currents are -0.06 A each; total I=-0.12 A. One-quarter of the area at -600 and three-quarters at -200 gives the mean -300 A/m^2. Exact synthetic data; numerical-only tolerance.

references.method: Independent cancellation identity: two equal 0.001 m^2 patches with +10 and -10 A/m^2 carry equal opposite currents, hence zero spatial mean while local densities remain nonzero. Exact synthetic data; numerical-only tolerance.
references.provenance: Curator limiting/cancellation check for the derived mean; no assertion of a zero local field.

relationship.original_equation: Source: I = surface integral of J_vector dot dA_vector. Introduced definition: J_mean_n = (surface integral of J_vector dot n_hat dA)/A = I/A.
relationship.translation_notes: Introduce J_mean_n as a spatial area mean of the normal component. A is total physical surface area; I is the oriented flux in the source integral. The executable expression evaluates the derived mean from known total current; it does not integrate an unknown field. Dimensions [I]/[A]=I L^-2, unit A/m^2. Signed I makes the mean signed; the textbook magnitude J=I/A is a special uniform normal-flow case. A local J vector, its magnitude and this area mean must not share an unqualified quantity identifier. No numerical constants occur. This definition is reusable independently of microscopic carrier models.

sources.evidence: Define J_mean_n as the area average of J dot the unit normal. Using the source total-current flux gives J_mean_n=I/A. This introduces an independently meaningful spatial mean; it does not assert local uniformity.

assumptions: Source carrier-counting model: uniform number density, one carrier charge and a well-defined average drift through the segment (Fig. 9.10 derivation).

Application profile: uniform normal transport of one species, or its separately isolated current contribution, in a material rest frame. No ohmic voltage-current assumption is required for this kinematic relationship.

The temperature/material conditions needed for n must be supplied. The source copper example assumes one mobile electron per atom; that assumption is confined to the example and is not a reusable material default.

gaps: Add m^-3, C, m^2, m/s, A and meanings charge_carrier_number_density, charge_per_carrier and normal_carrier_drift_velocity. Reuse prior electric_current and cross_sectional_area where the same support/frame and DC state match.
Do not alias charge_per_carrier to net_transferred_electric_charge, or signed drift velocity to a speed magnitude. Carrier species and material-frame compatibility require contextual validation.

models.inverse_notes: Forward v_d=I/(n*q*A) requires n>0,A>0,q!=0; I=0 gives unique v_d=0. Solve I given n,q,A,v_d: I=n*q*A*v_d; original guards remain and v_d may be zero. At n=5e20 m^-3,q=3.2e-19 C,A=2e-6 m^2,v_d=1 m/s, I=0.00032 A and forward substitution gives 1. Solve n given I,q,A,v_d: n=I/(q*A*v_d), requiring q!=0,A>0,v_d!=0 and recovered n>0. Solve A given I,n,q,v_d: A=I/(n*q*v_d), requiring n>0,q!=0,v_d!=0 and recovered A>0. Solve q given I,n,A,v_d: q=I/(n*A*v_d), requiring n>0,A>0,v_d!=0 and recovered q!=0, with a physically compatible species charge. The same numerical tuple recovers n=5e20,A=2e-6,q=3.2e-19 and each substitutes to 1 m/s. For any of these three parameter inverses, I=v_d=0 leaves the target undetermined within its original domain; v_d=0 with I!=0 is inconsistent. v_d!=0 with I=0 returns an excluded zero target. These are unique algebraic values when nonsingular, not causal or statistical identification. If the species is known, q is physically fixed and its inverse is only a consistency calculation; if several parameters are unknown, current/drift data alone are insufficient. No positive-root convention is used.
limitations: For several carrier species, total current is a sum of their signed contributions; one effective n or q cannot be inserted without justification. Spatial variation requires an integral or an explicitly defined compatible average.
Drift velocity is an ensemble mean, not thermal speed or electrical signal speed. This record does not predict mobility, scattering, field response or a transient.

The source example rounds its diameter before reporting area and alternates magnitude language with signed charge. The numerical check uses its reported area and signed result, with explicit interpretation; it does not silently recompute a different geometry.

references.method: Published -4.54e-4 m/s is retained. Use the source reported n, signed q and area, not a recomputed diameter. Conservative half-last-digit input bounds are I +/-0.05 A (20.0 in the problem), n +/-0.005e28 m^-3, |q| +/-0.005e-19 C and A +/-0.005e-6 m^2. Interval propagation plus 0.005e-4 m/s output rounding gives less than 4.04e-6 m/s; tolerance is 4.1e-6. Source q is a rounded example value, not a new measurement of elementary charge.
references.provenance: openstax-carrier-drift, Example 9.3; published calculated electron velocity, not experimental validation of a specimen.

references.method: Independent transport construction: synthetic carriers advance 0.5 m in 0.5 s, so mean v_d=1 m/s. The swept 1e-6 m^3 contains 5e14 carriers; at a stipulated positive charge 3.2e-19 C per carrier they transport 0.00016 C in 0.5 s, giving the input current 0.00032 A. Expected comes from displacement/time, not executing the inverse equation. Ideal rounded species data treated as exact numerical inputs; tolerance is numerical only.
references.provenance: Curator charge-counting derivation for a stipulated positive carrier species; no named material calibration or elementary-charge determination.

references.method: Limiting identity: zero net current in the declared single-species uniform model gives zero mean drift. Random microscopic motion can persist. Synthetic exact boundary; numerical-only tolerance.
references.provenance: Curator equilibrium check; this inference would fail for unseparated compensating currents from multiple species.

rejection_cases.reason: Neutral carriers cannot supply this electrical current; q is an original denominator exclusion.
Without a carrier population, the mean species velocity is not determined; zero/zero is not accepted.
Zero transverse area is excluded and makes the original denominator vanish.
Carrier species charge must be supplied; electron charge is not silently assumed.

relationship.original_equation: I = n q A v_d; source Eq. 9.4 gives v_d = I/(n q A); vector form J_vector = n q v_d_vector.
relationship.translation_notes: Local n,q,A,I retain source meanings; v_d is explicitly the signed normal component of the mean carrier velocity. This interpretation is supported by the source vector equation and its negative-electron example, despite earlier prose using the word magnitude. For uniform normal transport, project J_vector=n q v_d_vector onto the section normal and integrate to recover I=n q A v_d. [I]/([n][q][A])=A/((m^-3)*(A s)*(m^2))=m/s. No physical constant is inlined: q varies with species and charge state. For a fixed known species, its charge is a supplied physical parameter, not a free fit coefficient. Original exclusions n!=0,q!=0,A!=0 are retained as n>0, q*q>0, A>0. The guard product q*q enforces nonzero signed charge; it is not a square-root solve.
